title: Conjecture record
description: One mathematical conjecture. There is deliberately no `solved` boolean and no single `status` field: status is derived at build time from the append-only `claims` list. See docs/DATA-MODEL.md.

id.description: Canonical slug, stable forever. Never reused, never renamed.

title.description: Human-readable name, e.g. 'Erdős Problem 1' or 'Jacobian conjecture'.

aliases.description: Other names this conjecture is known by. Collatz alone has eight.

informal.description: Natural-language statement, LaTeX permitted. May be null when the upstream license forbids redistributing the text; link out instead.

formal.description: Machine-checkable statements. A formal statement is the trusted base for verification, so each one needs a named reviewer before it can gate a proof.

path.description: Path in this repo to the canonical challenge statement, if we host one.

theorem.description: Fully-qualified declaration name of the target theorem.

toolchain.description: Pinned mathlib tag or equivalent. Formalizations rot; record what it compiled against.

reviewed_by.description: Human who confirmed this statement faithfully expresses the informal one. Null means unreviewed; unreviewed statements must not gate a verified proof.

definition_hole.description: True when the challenge asks the solver to supply a definition (e.g. `def Answer : Prop := sorry`). These are auto-gameable by defining the hole to be the conjecture and closing with `rfl`, so they always require human review.

msc.description: Mathematics Subject Classification codes, top-level or finer.

ids.description: The crosswalk. The same conjecture exists under many identifiers in many databases and almost nothing links them; this field is the reason this project exists.

openness_basis.description: Why we believe this is open, and on whose authority. In October 2025 an AI lab announced ten solved Erdős problems that were in fact already solved in the literature; the curator's own definition of 'open' was 'I am personally unaware of a paper solving this'. This field makes that caveat structural instead of a footnote.

meaning.description: no_published_solution_known_to_curator is the honest default and means exactly what it says: absence of evidence from one source, not evidence of absence.

claims.description: Append-only. Never edit or delete a claim: to withdraw one, set its state to 'retracted' and add a new claim. The history is the point.

provenance.description: Per-field attribution and licensing. Upstream sources fragment across Apache-2.0, CC BY-SA and noncommercial terms, so we track this per field rather than per file.

fields.description: Dotted paths this attribution covers, e.g. 'statement.informal'.

license.description: SPDX identifier where possible, e.g. Apache-2.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0.

upstream_version.description: Commit, tag or snapshot date of the upstream source.

type.description: resolved_by_prior_literature exists specifically to distinguish 'someone proved this' from 'someone found the existing proof'. Conflating those two caused the October 2025 Erdős incident.

scope.description: Which part of the conjecture this claim settles. The Jacobian conjecture is false for n >= 3 and open for n = 2, so a claim that omits scope is often wrong.

evidence_tier.description: Strictly ordered. machine_verified means a proof assistant kernel checked it against our canonical statement; it is the only tier no human opinion can grant. An LLM review is never a tier of its own and can never promote a claim.

asserted_on.description: When the claimant made the claim.

quote.description: Short excerpt supporting the claim. Keep it short; some sources restrict redistribution.

reviewer.description: Named human who assessed this claim. Required for any tier above unverified_claim. Automation may never fill this in.

verification.description: Machine-check receipt. Present if and only if evidence_tier is machine_verified.

supersedes.description: Claim id this one replaces, for retractions and corrections.

then.description: A machine_verified claim must carry its receipt so anyone can reproduce the check.
Human tiers require a named human.

proof_path.description: Path to the accepted solution file in this repo.

statement_path.description: Canonical challenge statement the proof was checked against.

permitted_axioms.description: Allowlist used. Denylisting axiom names is wrong since Lean 4.29, which emits a uniquely-named axiom per native_decide call.

run_url.description: CI run that produced this result.
